# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶1:** All these incomplete and monstrous formations of falsity and evil—among them the chief ruling falsity and the evil love conjoined to it, together with the subsidiary evils they served [GAP-1]—these are what shaped the human will and understanding. How did they discover the form of the Divine Human impressed upon their nature, even though when that form was displayed to the prior states of evil from which they derived, they did not yet exist? They never beheld the Divine Truth made manifest! And how did they take the authentic imprint of the form of the Divine Truth? They imposed it upon [GAP-2] the will and understanding of the natural human.

**¶2:** The proprium that issued forth from the ruling evils, which is the corporeal-sensual nature, rose up toward the form of the Divine Truth made manifest. It was severed from that elevated state and descended into the external natural mind, for the interior degrees of the mind did not receive it. When it descended into the external natural, it formed a perception. It established itself within that natural knowledge and produced apparent works. And when [GAP-3] the incomplete formations of falsity fell [GAP-4] into the external natural, into the outermost degree, at the [GAP-5] time [GAP-6]

**¶3:** [GAP-7] those apparent works, the proprium assumed them and spoke through the ruling evil, their chief. It says to its companion evils: Come! Surrender to me your remaining light of wisdom, and I will construct for you a form after the likeness of the Divine. What it commanded, they did: they surrendered their wisdom to it, and it constructed [GAP-8].

**¶4:** The proprium that i[GAP-9]ssued forth—which is the corporeal-sensual nature that beheld the form of the Divine Truth made manifest and that formed a perception and was established within it—afterwards it rose up through the [GAP-10] apparent works. It entered into the ruling evils [GAP-11] they formed the human will and understanding after the [GAP-12] likeness of the Divine. Through the energy of the proprium that had beheld the form of the Divine Truth, it entered the ruling evils [GAP-13] through the apparent works. It assumed them and they too fashioned [GAP-14] and each brought forth according to its hereditary nature [GAP-15]; some resembling the Divine form, some not.

**¶6:** The formative power implanted within the will and understanding of the natural human both external and internal faculties for perception and activity. It was apportioned domain by domain. For everything that the perceptions and constituent elements receive from without, there exist interior memories, repositories, and chambers; and what is received into them is stored there. Whenever these faculties are called upon concerning what is deposited in their interior memories, they bring forth what they received within and present it to the inquiring faculty that requested it of them.

**¶7:** In this manner its faculty [GAP-16] through the outer [GAP-17] capacities of perception, to behold [GAP-18] every kind of influx with[GAP-19]in the mind.

**¶8:** Also, the faculty of intellectual sight [GAP-20] has its own domains and chambers and repositories and memories within, so that every form it may perceive—whether of good or evil, whether of heavenly love or of what is detestable or of concupiscence—it can receive into its memories and repositories. Also, when the faculty of intellectual sight is disposed to bring forth the form that it perceived and took in, it can enter into its memories [GAP-21] at the time and reflect upon and search [GAP-22] and it brings it forth [GAP-23] and presents it to the inquiring faculty that requested it and the one that desired it—whether it be something from concu[GAP-24]piscence or a form of love [GAP-25] or something hateful. And thus shall that faculty of intellectual sight produce and accomplish what it does in each domain.

**¶9:** The faculty of obedient reception has its own memories also. Every doctrine or communication it may receive, whether of good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its domains and interior repositories, and it is guarded in its [GAP-26] for an entire cycle of states. After a full cycle, if an inquiring faculty comes and asks about the doctrine that it received [GAP-27] at that time and took into its memories, immediately it shall enter its repositories and seek and review and search after this truth, and bring it forth from where it was first deposited, the place in which it was preserved.

**¶10:** [GAP-28] In like order, the faculty of perceiving spiritual quality shall function just as that of intellectual sight and that of obedient reception. Every interior quality it discerns it shall take in [GAP-29] to itself and deposit in its interior memories. Every time it is asked by an inquiring faculty, it shall enter [GAP-30] and [GAP-31] its memory and recall [GAP-32] only these things.

**¶11:** However, even the capacity of outward expression and the communicating faculty within it, and the faculty of experiential discernment, have a power dwelling in them. Again, that faculty of experiential discernment has chambers and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these experiential knowledges and gathers them in. And at any moment when inquiry is made concerning a quality of experience, if [GAP-33] it shall send it forth and recall that experiential knowledge. It shall capture and present even the character of that experience; it gives its memory to the inquiring faculty that asks for it.

**¶12:** Again, the faculty of direct conjunction and appropriation is also thus: When it makes contact with its object, that contact shall receive its memory. And it [GAP-34] takes it into its interior repository [GAP-35] until someone asks this faculty for the memory. [GAP-36] Immediately, it shall enter again and bring forth the memory of this conjunction that it effected, and give it to whoever asks for it.

**¶13:** And the faculty of the will that rules over them all is far more like this than any other. Everything that these five modes of reception take in and store for the will, it shall receive and guard. Any time they ask for what they deposited, it shall bring forth and give everything that they entrusted to it.

**¶14:** For the counsel of the will is like the ruling love. All the subordinate affections of its doctrine and the governing thoughts of its power are placed with it. Any time its governing thoughts entreat it for whatever they seek, it shall give them the counsel and direction by which they act.

**¶15:** Furthermore, it is like a steward of interior goods: Everything that is entrusted to it and given to it by them, it shall receive and place in separate containing forms and domains. Any time [GAP-37]

**¶16:** [GAP-38] in the domain where it deposited it.

**¶17:** This also is the manner of the faculty of the external natural mind. The perception that the understanding beholds and gives to it, and it receives it—it shall bring it forth again from the memories wherein it had placed it, and give it to whoever asks for it.

**¶18:** Again, [GAP-39] the doctrine that the faculty of obedient reception hears and gives to it, and it receives it from them—at any time when inquiry is made concerning that doctrine, it shall bring it forth and give the communication of obedient reception to whoever has asked. It shall bring forth and give the communication of obedient reception to whoever has asked.

**¶19:** Again, [GAP-40] the faculty of perceiving interior quality follows this same pattern; and that of experiential discernment is of the same kind. The direct appropriation by the capacities of conjunctio[GAP-41]n—they shall bring it forth into [GAP-42] and whenever inquiry is made, it shall bring it forth and give it.

**¶20:** Indeed, guardian truths stand at these openings of reception, protecting them, and confirmations of doctrine are fastened upon the openings under the authority of the guardian truths that protect them!

**¶21:** Just as guardian truths protect an ordered arrangement of the mind with elevated doctrinal insights and stations of spiritual vigilance. As the inner chambers proceed from there and the confirmations are upon the entrances, the guardian truths control the confirmations of the entrances while they abide at the threshold [GAP-43] of the stations of vigilance. So, an affection or truth that belongs to the mind's own doctrine as a genuine constituent of it, belonging to its own spiritual territory—for such the guardians shall open the entrance and receive it in willingly. However, the foreign influx that comes—they shall prevent it, and leave it standing at the entrance. They shall not yield to let it enter. Again, another influx that they will eventually receive—with great difficulty before [GAP-44] they admit it, you shall find many inner chambers [GAP-45] that [GAP-46] there are a multitude [GAP-47] of them. The number of confirming closures [GAP-48] are [GAP-49] Whenever someone wishes [GAP-50] the confirmations at hand, opens the entrance and brings forth whoever is hidden within.

**¶22:** This external natural mind is like the mighty ordered arrangement for spiritual combat. And the entrances of the ordered mind with their guardians are like the openings and faculties of the external person. Now, the openings of the external person are those of intellectual sight, of obedient reception, and of perceiving quality; and those that send forth expressions of thought. There are many vigilant truths and a multitude of guardian principles placed over the faculties of the external person, protecting its openings. And the ruling faculty within it is the directive of the external person, the sovereign love of the entire ordered mind; so that whenever it wills it can open, or when it wills it can close.

**¶23:** However, if and when the Divine Rational Truth descends, it shall turn toward the openings of the external natural mind. The ruling evils, who are the guardians of the entrances, shall hinder and restrain it from entering. They shall bind the circuit of the external mind so that the Divine influx cannot enter it.

**¶24:** Nevertheless, the Divine Rational Truth by its wisdom and holy reverence and diligent power shall humble the ruling evils that are set at the mind's openings. When it finishes humbling them it shall take from them the means of closing every opening of the external mind. Now, the openings that had been opened before to the processions of concupiscence, to receive the perceptions of sensual delight, to transmit the expressions of worldly preoccupation, to receive the experiential pleasures of various natural satisfactions and impure indulgences together with the proprium within them—whoever ceases to receive these, his will and thought shall follow after the Divine.

**¶25:** So now, because the confirmations governing the external nature of the regenerate person are in the possession of the Divine Rational Truth within, he is open [GAP-51] to receive all that is pleasing to the Divine. He is open to take in through his understanding the perceptions of lov[GAP-52]e and righteousness.

**¶27:** Simply, all openings of the mind were in like manner opening at one time to evil, but now have opened to good. The proprium was ruling in the external nature at that time, doing whatever it desired, having no higher authority in command.

**¶28:** Yet now, authority has been taken from the proprium in the faculties of the external nature. The Divine Proceeding Good has become lord over all its capacities. It has bound them with the bond of heavenly order, and sealed them with the confirmation of divine truth. It has opened the openings of the external mind to the good, and because of this the good enters them through obedient reception and through the understanding. It dwells in the will. The Divine Truth Proceeding reigns. It accomplishes all that it purposes. It annuls [GAP-53] the purpose of the proprium, from first principles to last effects. [GAP-54] In contrast, the purpose of the [GAP-55] Divine Truth Pro[GAP-56]ceeding comes to fulfillment, together with the direction of the Divine Rational.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: All [these a]bortions, amongst them are Saklas and his consort and the ones whom they have served [ ... ], they are the ones that shaped Adam and Eve. How did they find this beautiful image laid over their shape, even though when it was displayed to their fathers they were not in existence? They never saw the image of the Ambassador! And how did they take the seal of the image of the Ambassador? They added it to [the] shape of Adam and Eve.

The Sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is the Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [ ... / ... ]

[When the Sin was in the] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [the image].

The Sin that s[purted out ... / ... ] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits and assumed them]. It went in to the rulers [and spoke in them, and] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the Sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted the image, and they] begat each of them according to his destiny [ ... ]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.

The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
In this way his faculty [works through the] outer [limbs] to look at [and to receive] every type with [in the body]

Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [after it] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[st and desire, or a]n image of love [or ... / ... something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.

The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [stores] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.

[In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [and seek] and [search its] storehouse and remember [and bring out] only these things.

However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [someone asks for it] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.

Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.

And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.

For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.
Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [ ... / ... / ... ]
[It shall find it] in the place that it put it.

This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.

Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.

Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds ... / ... ] they shall bring it out in to [ ... / ... ] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!

Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [ ... / ... ] that [ ... ] there are a mass [ ... / ... ] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [ ... ] are [ ... ] Whenever someone will wish [to release] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.

This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.

However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.

Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the Sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.

So, now, bec[ause] the b[olt]s to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light M[in]d within, he is open [to receive] in all that is pleasing to God. He is op[en to take] in by his eyes the visions of lov[e and truth] and righteousness.

[S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.

Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [s]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Holy Spir][it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.

fills.explanation: The article "the" is grammatically required before "shape of Adam and Eve," and the spiritual reading confirms "upon the will and understanding."
The article "the" is grammatically required before "abortions fell," referring to the previously introduced abortions.
The preposition "to" is required for "fell to the ground," and the spiritual reading confirms the downward motion to the external natural.

In the Manichaean cosmological sequence, the abortions fell to earth at the second time, after the first creation of the tree; the spiritual reading's "at the [GAP-5] time" confirms a sequential marker.

fills.explanation: Paragraph 3 begins the scene where the Sin/proprium, having established itself in the fruits (apparent works), assumes the rulers; the parallel in ¶4 confirms "it came up in the fruits" and the spiritual reading says the proprium was in the apparent works.
The ruler promised "I will construct for you an image after the likeness of the exalted one," so the completion of this promise is "he constructed the image."
Paragraph 4 recapitulates ¶3 where "in the fruits, it assumed them"; the Sin rose up in the fruits and assumed them before entering the rulers.
Parallel to ¶3 where the Sin "spoke in the ruler, their leader" and commanded them; in ¶4's summary the Sin entered the rulers and spoke in them, prompting them to form Adam and Eve.
This directly echoes the phrase in ¶3: "an image after the likeness of the exalted one," and the spiritual reading confirms "after the likeness of the Divine."
The spiritual reading confirms the Sin entered the rulers "through the apparent works" (fruits), and "It" begins the next clause where it assumed them; the editor's reading is correct.
The rulers "too sculpted the image" parallels the construction in ¶3/¶8; "and they" begins the clause "they begat each of them" as confirmed by the spiritual reading's "and each brought forth."
The spiritual reading says "its faculty [GAP-16] through the outer capacities," indicating the faculty operates through the outer limbs; "works through the" fits the expository register.
The Kephalaia consistently uses "limbs" for the bodily members/organs of perception, and the spiritual reading's "capacities of perception" corresponds to "limbs" in the natural register.

Paragraph 6 establishes the faculties serve dual purposes "for perception and activity"; the outer limbs both perceive (look at) and receive, so "and to receive" completes the standard paired function described throughout the chapter.
The spiritual reading says "within the mind," and the Kephalaia's natural-plane equivalent for the mind's domain is "the body"; "within the body" completes the description of where perception occurs.
The verb "has" is required to predicate the faculty's possession of "houses and cavities and repositories," confirmed by the spiritual reading.
The temporal phrase "at the time" is required to indicate when the faculty enters its storehouses to retrieve, confirmed by the spiritual reading.
The parallel in ¶9 has "seek and review and search after this word"; "after it" completes the searching action, meaning the faculty seeks after the stored image.
The conjunction "and" connects "brings it out" to "gives it," forming the standard retrieval-and-delivery sequence found throughout the chapter.

Completing "lust" and adding the common Manichaean doublet "lust and desire" before the disjunction "or an image of love"; this expands the category of concupiscence as the spiritual reading indicates.

The paragraph's established vocabulary includes "houses," "repositories," and "stores"; "guarded in its stores" parallels ¶8's list of storage terms and fits the spiritual reading's "cycle of states" guarding period.
The temporal preposition "at" is required for "at this time," referring to the moment the sound was received, confirmed by the spiritual reading.
The prepositional phrase "In like order" introduces the next faculty parallel, matching the structural pattern of the chapter.
The reflexive "to it" completes "take in to it" meaning the faculty receives the odour into itself, matching the reception pattern of the other senses.
Paralleling ¶9's "go into its repositories and seek and review and search," the faculty goes in and seeks; "and seek" continues the retrieval action sequence.
Continuing the seek-and-search pattern from ¶9 ("seek and review and search"), "search its storehouse" describes the faculty reviewing its memory store.

The parallel in ¶9 completes the retrieval sequence with "send it out from where it was first put"; "remember and bring out only these things" follows this established pattern of recall followed by retrieval.
Following the pattern established in ¶9 ("if someone comes and asks that faculty"), the conditional clause requires a questioner prompting retrieval of the stored taste.
The verb "takes" describes the faculty receiving and storing the memory of touch into its repository, consistent with the reception pattern of all five senses.
The temporal conjunction "until" marks the period of storage before retrieval is requested, matching the pattern of all other sense-faculty descriptions.
The adverb "Immediately" matches ¶9's identical usage ("immediately it shall go into its repositories"), indicating the prompt retrieval response.
Following the cellarman metaphor of ¶15 about storing and retrieving deposits, the conclusion states that the faculty shall find the item in the place where it was deposited.
The article "the" introduces "the sound that the ears will hear," following the established pattern of each sense-faculty paragraph opening.
The article "the" introduces "the faculty of smell," following the same pattern as ¶18's "the sound" and ¶8's "the faculty of the eyes."
The genitive "of" connects "entrance" to "the watchposts," indicating the guards sit at the entrance belonging to the watchposts/stations of vigilance.
The pronoun "they" refers to the guards who, with great difficulty, eventually admit certain visitors; confirmed by the spiritual reading "before they admit it."
The action on the bolts/confirmations is to loosen or release them in order to open the gate, corresponding to removing the confirming closures that seal the entrance.
The infinitive "to receive" expresses the regenerate person's openness to receive all that pleases God, matching the chapter's theme of open receptivity after the Light Mind takes control.

Completing "love" and adding "and truth" before "and righteousness" yields the triad love-truth-righteousness, corresponding to good of the will, truth of the understanding, and their conjunction in life.
The article "the" is grammatically required before "will of sin," and the spiritual reading confirms "the purpose of the proprium."
The contrastive phrase sets up the opposition between the annulled will of sin and the fulfilled will of the Holy Spirit, confirmed by the spiritual reading.

Correcting the editor's typo "Holly" to "Holy"; "Holy Spirit" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane term for what corresponds to the Divine Truth Proceeding, as confirmed two sentences earlier in the same paragraph.
Completing "Spirit" (Holy Spirit), which is the established term in ¶28; the spiritual reading's "Divine Truth Proceeding" confirms this is the correct entity.
